rules.requirement: Execution topology declarations may request device count/mesh/parallelism, but Host Resource Broker remains admission, placement, reservation and lease authority.
MAX provider-local queues/batching/prefill/decode scheduling may optimize an admitted invocation, but SHALL NOT become global FA3 scheduling authority.
Portable kernel semantics and each target-specific compiled artifact SHALL have distinct identities linked by lineage.
Hardware/target specialization SHALL preserve canonical workload semantics; semantic drift requires a new canonical artifact/contract identity and evidence.
Model support claims SHALL NOT promote a model variant; compatibility evidence MUST bind model variant, provider version and hardware profile.
Compiled execution artifacts MUST bind model artifact, provider version, compiler version, target architecture, kernel set and compilation config.
Warm-cache artifacts MUST be scoped to compiled artifact/model variant/provider/compiler/target/config identity and SHALL invalidate on incompatible drift.
Cache ownership, scope and lifecycle MUST be explicit.
Cancellation/abort MUST release provider-local reservations and cache resources; leak behavior fails closed.
Shared KV/cache state MUST preserve tenant/security context boundaries and MUST NOT cross incompatible model/provider/config identities.
Performance evidence MUST bind provider/model/hardware/execution topology/parallelism/warm-state identity.
OpenAI-compatible MAX endpoints are serving projections only and SHALL NOT become the FA3 model-routing authority.
Stable and nightly/development provider states MUST have independent evidence; one channel SHALL NOT satisfy promotion for another.
Source availability SHALL NOT imply production-use or redistribution authorization; licence admission remains explicit and fail-closed.
